Approach

How I build an ad set

The same four steps for any brand. The ads below are what the steps produce once the buyer, the levers and the test plan are agreed.

01Learn the buyer first

Audience, price band and product range before the first headline. Here that is style-led buyers aged 22 to 38 in the Netherlands, with an ear for music, shopping a €85 to €295 range.

02Pick the lever, then write

Every ad keeps the brand's existing tone of voice and adds a psychological lever and two emotional triggers to it. The copy follows the lever, so each variant tests a separate idea.

03Build the system once

A fixed look and live layouts keep a large set of variants on brand. Each brand's real product photos go into the designs, so a new product or market only needs new inputs.

04Test one variable at a time

Each round has one variable, one primary read and one guardrail. The winner carries forward and the next idea has to beat it.

The brand

Premium leather, made in numbered runs

Hide Fidelity is a premium leather brand from Amsterdam. Every piece is 100% leather, finished with cobalt thread and made in small numbered runs. Boots, shoes, bags and belts for people who value detail and like their style a little bold.

Catalogue

Six pieces, one range

Layouts

One system, four layouts

The brand signals below never change. One layout carries each phase, so the product stays the loudest thing on screen.

LookClean and flat

Flat colour field, one hero object, headline on solid strips. Black leather, cobalt stitching, no models and no lifestyle clutter.

TypeStrip headline, mono catalogue

Big Shoulders Display in caps on solid strips, IBM Plex Mono for catalogue numbers and support lines. Six words or fewer in the headline.

VoiceShort, confident, plain

Wordplay only where it earns its place. Scarcity appears only when a real numbered run exists.

PlacementsInstagram feed 4:5, Stories and Reels 9:16

Every cell is sized for the placement it runs in. Text stays out of the top 14% and bottom 20% of vertical frames. Placements are set by hand while testing.

Targeting baseInterests, then behaviour

Music, festivals, streetwear, vintage, premium fashion, leather footwear. Lookalikes from purchasers once there are 500 or more.

LanguagePlain English, euro pricing

International English for a Dutch market. Euro prices, EU sizing, delivery and returns. Local references stay light.

Method

How a round is run

Meta A/B test

Meta splits the audience so cells never overlap. Dynamic creative mixes elements and hides which one won. Use it only after a winner exists, to polish copy.

Seven to thirty days per round

Seven days is the floor, so weekday and weekend behaviour both count. The round closes once each cell reaches its conversion target, within 30 days. Results in the first days are unstable, so no winner is called before the round closes.

Equal budget per cell

Cells share the round budget evenly. A cell needs roughly 25 to 50 of its target event before it is read.

Winners carry forward as messages

Meta reports how likely the winning cell is to win again. A low score counts as a tie, and the current winner stays.

Optimise on a proxy when thin

Early rounds optimise on landing page views or add-to-cart. Purchases need about 50 a week before Meta learns on them.

Scale with the winners

Once round 8 closes, the winning creative from each phase moves into the live campaigns.
